lines.text: Diamond moves heat better than silver.
It carries heat about five times better than copper or silver.
Heat moves through it as vibrations in tightly bonded carbon atoms.
Yet most diamonds block electricity, the opposite of a metal.
Jewelers use that to test stones with a heated metal probe.
A diamond pulls heat from the tip fast, so the tip cools.
Cubic zirconia and glass pull heat away slowly, so they read differently.
Moissanite can pass a thermal test like diamond.
But under magnification it shows doubled facet edges.
Thermal testers for jewelers date from the late 1970s.

lines.text: Today diamond layers also help spread heat in power chips.

post.caption: Diamond moves heat better than silver. It carries heat about five times better than copper or silver, as vibrations in tightly bonded carbon atoms, yet most diamonds block electricity, the opposite of a metal. Jewelers use that to test stones with a heated metal probe, because a diamond pulls heat from the tip fast and the tip cools. Cubic zirconia and glass pull heat away slowly, so they read differently. Moissanite can pass a thermal test like diamond, but under magnification it shows doubled facet edges. Thermal testers for jewelers date from the late 1970s, and today diamond layers also help spread heat in power chips.
